_comment: NOT LOADED BY DEFAULT. These are worked examples, not working profiles.
Field indices below have NOT been confirmed against real output from the named apps, and
are very likely wrong: both QRScout and ScoutingPASS let each team configure their own
column order, so there may be no single correct answer for either.
Why they are not in bridge_profiles.json: detection refuses any payload that more than one
profile fits. A 6-column tab-separated payload fits both a generic profile and these, so
shipping them active would make the Bridge refuse ordinary payloads. Worse, if detection
resolved the tie instead of refusing, real QRScout data would seal under generic indices —
match and team read from the wrong columns, silently.
1. Export a real QR payload from your team's actual configuration.
2. Count the columns and correct the indices below.
3. Add `exactFields` set to your column count, so it cannot collide with a generic profile.
4. Verify a sealed record reads back the right team and match.
5. Set verified: true, and load this file alongside bridge_profiles.json.
Step 4 is not optional. A wrong index costs you a competition's scouting data and you will
not find out until you build a picklist on it.

profiles.name: QRScout (tab-separated) — EXAMPLE, indices unconfirmed
profiles.notes: Indices unconfirmed. QRScout's column order is team-configurable. Confirm against a real export before use.

profiles.name: ScoutingPASS (tab-separated) — EXAMPLE, indices unconfirmed
profiles.notes: Indices unconfirmed. ScoutingPASS is configured per team via a JSON config, so column order varies by deployment. Confirm against a real export before use.
